correctness.rationale: For all integers k>=3, the grounded graph Laplacian is positive definite. With the hub grounded, each untouched arm contributes trace 3, leaf grounding reduces to 1/2, intermediate grounding to 1, double grounding to 0; two leaves on distinct arms give exactly 3k-5. With the hub ungrounded, all possible three-leader patterns reduce to six arm-type orbits (III, IIV, IVV, VVV, B+I, B+V); their exact Schur-complement trace formula is derived, not assumed, and strict rational inequalities prove k=3 VVV, k=4 IVV and k>=5 hub+two leaves optimal. For k>=5, all six non-hub cost gaps are strictly positive. Separate direct rational inversions of the original grounded Laplacian corroborate 90 orbit examples and exhaustively 284 labeled triples at k=3,4,5; these are finite checks only.

value.rationale: This natural three-leader pinning design problem has three qualitatively different exact optimal structures as branch count increases: all outer leaves at k=3, a mixed intermediate–outer pattern at k=4, and a central leader plus peripheral spread at k>=5. Exact optimum costs and optimizer counts resolve the entire infinite family. The boundary at four arms cannot be inferred from degree rankings or from the earlier two-leader result, and it identifies when adding a hub leader is counterproductive.
